title: Biliary Cysts, Bismuth Classification, and Cholangiocarcinoma

steps.tx: Congenital disproportionate aneurysmal dilatation of the extrahepatic or intrahepatic biliary ductal tree is termed a **choledochal cyst**. Predominantly identified in female infants and young children, these anomalies stem from an abnormal pancreaticobiliary ductal junction. In this anomalous arrangement, the common bile duct joins the main pancreatic duct outside the duodenal wall beyond the protective control of the sphincter of Oddi.
steps.say: A choledochal cyst represents congenital dilatation of the bile ducts, frequently resulting from an anomalous junction of the pancreatic and bile ducts.

vis.alt: Anatomical schematic showing anatomical classifications of choledochal cysts and locations of cholangiocarcinoma.
vis.caption: Biliary ductal anomalies: congenital choledochal cysts and anatomical classification of cholangiocarcinoma. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The anomalous junction permits continuous reflux of pancreatic juice into the biliary tree, activating proenzymes that provoke chronic mural inflammation, epithelial dysplasia, and malignant transformation. Choledochal cysts are categorized into five types by the **Todani classification**. Type one, accounting for eighty to ninety percent of cases, comprises solitary fusiform or cystic dilatation of the extrahepatic common bile duct.
steps.say: The Todani classification divides choledochal cysts into five types, with type one representing fusiform extrahepatic dilatation in most cases.

steps.tx: Children classically present with the clinical triad of intermittent abdominal pain, right upper quadrant palpable mass, and jaundice, though all three features co-exist in only a minority. Because untreated cyst mucosa carries a lifetime risk of malignant transformation up to thirty percent, internal drainage alone is abandoned. The mandatory definitive surgery is total **cyst excision** accompanied by a Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy.
steps.say: Due to a substantial risk of cancer, choledochal cysts require complete surgical cyst excision and Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy reconstruction.

steps.tx: A rare variant characterized by non-obstructive saccular dilatation of intrahepatic bile ducts associated with congenital hepatic fibrosis is **Caroli disease**, designated as Todani type five. Patients develop recurrent bouts of bacterial cholangitis, intrahepatic stone formation, and portal hypertension. When intrahepatic ectasia is localized to a single hepatic lobe, anatomical hemihepatectomy is curative, whereas diffuse bilobar involvement necessitates orthotopic liver transplantation.
steps.say: Caroli disease involves congenital intrahepatic duct dilatation with hepatic fibrosis, managed by partial hepatectomy or liver transplantation.

steps.tx: The primary epithelial malignancy originating from the mucosal lining of the intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary system is **cholangiocarcinoma**. Major predisposing aetiological factors encompass primary sclerosing cholangitis, choledochal cysts, chronic Clonorchis sinensis or Opisthorchis viverrini liver fluke infection, and hepatolithiasis. Greater than ninety percent of lesions are well-differentiated, mucin-producing sclerosing adenocarcinomas characterized by dense desmoplastic stroma.
steps.say: Cholangiocarcinoma is a sclerosing adenocarcinoma of bile duct epithelium, linked to primary sclerosing cholangitis and liver fluke infestation.

vis.caption: Cholangiocarcinoma: intrahepatic, perihilar and distal bile duct tumours. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Anatomically, cholangiocarcinomas are categorized into intrahepatic, perihilar, and distal varieties. Perihilar lesions located in the main hepatic duct bifurcation account for over fifty percent of all occurrences. The standardized classification mapping longitudinal ductal extension of perihilar tumours is the **Bismuth classification**, also known as the Bismuth-Corlette system. This anatomical framework guides surgical resectability by detailing confluence involvement.
steps.say: The Bismuth classification maps perihilar cholangiocarcinomas according to ductal involvement relative to the primary hepatic bifurcation.

rows: Reaches primary confluence without sectoral spread

Bile duct excision + extended right hepatectomy
Involves confluence and left sectoral ducts

steps.tx: Surgical resection for Bismuth type three tumours mandates en bloc excision of the extrahepatic biliary tree, regional lymphadenectomy, and formal hemihepatectomy. Routine resection of the caudate lobe is obligatory because its independent biliary tributaries drain directly into the biliary confluence, harbouring frequent microscopic cancer extension. Portal vein involvement on the side of the retained liver remnant represents a principal contraindication to **curative resection**.
steps.say: Resection of perihilar cholangiocarcinoma requires hemihepatectomy and caudate lobectomy to ensure clean margins at the biliary confluence.

steps.tx: In advanced unresectable cholangiocarcinoma, management focuses on palliative alleviation of intractable pruritus and prevention of fatal ascending cholangitis. Decompression is accomplished through endoscopic or percutaneous placement of self-expanding metallic **biliary stents**. Unilateral drainage that opacifies and drains at least fifty percent of functional liver parenchyma is sufficient to resolve clinical jaundice and improve overall quality of life.
steps.say: Palliative management of unresectable cholangiocarcinoma relies on metallic stent placement to relieve obstructive jaundice and prevent cholangitis.

right.title: Self-Expanding Metal Stents
